**Santa Anita Race 1 — Sat., Sept. 26, 2026**

1:00 PM PT post; $50k maiden claiming; one mile on turf; 10-horse field. It's restricted to California-bred maidens.

**Consensus (3 handicappers)**

- DRF (Steve Andersen): Dr. Filkins, Doing Time, Going Nowhere
- BettingNews (Chris Adams): Going Nowhere, Doing Time, Daddys Star, Heroic Dose
- In the Money (Dean Keppler): Heroic Dose, Dr. Filkins, Doing Time

Doing Time is the only horse on all three lists. Going Nowhere, Dr. Filkins, and Heroic Dose each appear on two lists and each is one handicapper's top pick. Daddys Star is on only one list.

**Morning line (BettingNews):** Going Nowhere 9-5, Doing Time 3-1, Heroic Dose 4-1, Daddys Star 12-1. Dr. Filkins' morning line wasn't listed.

**Horse notes**

- **Doing Time:** He got caught in traffic on the turn on Sept. 7 and lost his momentum, in what was his 14th start. This is his first time running for a claiming price, and Umberto Rispoli rides him for the first time. Knock: he has had many chances to win already.
- **Going Nowhere:** He has run second in four of eight turf starts and is often in front in the stretch, but he hasn't gotten the win yet. Dropping back into a maiden claimer for the first time since March helps. He is the likely favorite and a chronic runner-up.
- **Dr. Filkins:** He clipped heels on the turn on Aug. 8 and finished sixth. Juan Hernandez rides him Saturday, and he has had three half-mile workouts for trainer Sean McCarthy in the past five weeks. This is his second start back from a layoff. He is the possible value play since no odds were posted.
- **Heroic Dose:** He is coming off two straight second-place finishes in turf routes at this level for trainer Mullins, and this third start of his form cycle could be his best.
- **Daddys Star:** He ran at this same level last time out. He is the price horse at 12-1.

**Pace:** Dr. Filkins and Doing Time come from off the pace and will be chasing Going Nowhere and Daddys Star, who are expected to run near the front. If the two speed horses press each other, that helps the closers.

**How this could shape a card**

- **Win:** Going Nowhere is the chalk, but his habit of finishing second argues for using him underneath rather than betting him to win at a short price. Dr. Filkins and Heroic Dose are win alternatives with better value.
- **Exacta or trifecta top:** Doing Time, Going Nowhere, Dr. Filkins, Heroic Dose.
- **Bottom spots or saver:** Daddys Star.
- BettingNews played Going Nowhere to win and a trifecta with Going Nowhere and Doing Time on top, over those two plus Daddys Star and Heroic Dose.

Check for scratches and final odds before post.

**Santa Anita Race 2, Saturday, Sept. 26, 2026**

The race is a $16,000 claimer at 6½ furlongs on dirt with five runners, post time 1:33 PM PT. One site listed a different race condition for Race 2, but three other sources agree on these details.

**Consensus: Piper's Causeway is the top choice**

- **VSiN:** Piper's Causeway, then B Grayson, then Gypsy Tears
- **BettingNews:** Piper's Causeway, then Naftis, then B Grayson, then Gypsy Tears. Their suggested plays are a win bet on the top pick at 5-2 or better, and an exacta keying Piper's Causeway and Naftis over the rest of the field.
- **Ultimate Capper:** Naftis on top
- **Pick Pony Edge Radar:** Piper's Causeway flagged as a value play, with a morning line of 2-1 and a value score of 6/10

**Morning line:** B Grayson 7-5, Piper's Causeway 2-1, Gypsy Tears 4-1, Naftis 9-2 (odds per BettingNews).

**Contenders**

**Piper's Causeway (2-1).** This is the pace horse. Pick Pony says there are no other front-runners in the race, so he should get an easy, uncontested lead. His most recent dirt start was a win at Santa Anita last October. Over the summer he ran sixth and seventh in two statebred allowance races on turf at five furlongs, racing on or near the lead. Dropping back to dirt and to this lower class should help. Pick Pony also notes that his trainer has shown a flat-bet profit this year.

**B Grayson (7-5).** He will likely be the post-time favorite. On Sept. 11 at Los Alamitos, he won a $20,000 claimer for horses that had not yet won three races, rallying wide from last of eight at 5½ furlongs. He won a $25,000 claimer at six furlongs at Santa Anita in May with the same closing style. The concern is that he is a closer in a race with only one speed horse.

**Naftis (9-2).** He is the likeliest horse to pressure the leader. He breaks from the rail and has shown speed at times, but he has lost his last six starts and his last win was a sprint at Golden Gate Fields in 2024. On the positive side, he is trained by Kimura and ridden by Vallejo, one of the top combinations on the circuit. Two of the four sources rank him second or better.

**Gypsy Tears (4-1).** He breaks from the outside post. He ran a dull fourth of six as the 7-5 favorite in a starter allowance at Los Alamitos on Sept. 13, but he has won three times in the last year and runs from off the pace. He is a candidate for the bottom of exotic tickets.

**How the race should set up**

With so little speed, Piper's Causeway should control the pace unless Naftis goes with him from the rail. B Grayson and Gypsy Tears both need a fast early pace to close into, and they are unlikely to get one. The race looks tailored to Piper's Causeway.

**Betting card ideas**

- **Win:** Piper's Causeway, if he is 2-1 or better. This is the strongest consensus play.
- **Exacta:** Piper's Causeway on top, with B Grayson and Naftis underneath. Add a smaller saver with B Grayson on top of Piper's Causeway, since B Grayson will be the favorite.
- **Exacta box:** Piper's Causeway, B Grayson, and Naftis.
- **Trifecta:** Piper's Causeway on top, B Grayson and Naftis second, and all others third.
- **Value angle:** If B Grayson is bet down to even money or lower, the edge on Piper's Causeway grows.

**Cautions:** Five-horse fields often pay small exotics, and scratches could change the race shape. Check the odds and the track condition near post time.

**Santa Anita Race 3: City of Hope Mile (G2), 1 mile turf, 6 runners, Sat 9/26/26**

Race 3 is the City of Hope Mile, a Breeders' Cup Mile prep. Post time is 2:06 PM PT. Most of the field comes out of the Grade 2 Del Mar Mile on Aug. 22, where only a half-length separated the first four finishers.

**Consensus (4 handicappers)**
- **King of Gosford:** in every top 3, and one source's top pick. Likely favorite.
- **El Potente:** in every top 3, and one source's top pick.
- **Detain:** top pick of DRF's Steve Andersen and of Jeremy Plonk.
- **Irish Aces:** in two sources' top 3 or 4, often as the secondary contender.
- **Cabo Spirit:** one mention, mainly as the pace factor.
- **Teao:** Andersen's live longshot for a minor placing.

**Individual selections**
- *Steve Andersen (DRF/VSiN):* Detain, King of Gosford, El Potente
- *Jeremy Plonk (Xpressbet):* Detain, El Potente, King of Gosford
- *BettingNews:* King of Gosford, Irish Aces, El Potente, Cabo Spirit, with King of Gosford as best bet of the card
- *Jarrod Horak (Runaway Horse):* El Potente and King of Gosford as primary, with Irish Aces and Detain as secondary

**Key angles**
- **Detain:** He closed with a rush to lose the Del Mar Mile by a head in his American stakes debut, but needs Cabo Spirit and possibly others to set a decent pace. Plonk says a very slow second quarter hurt him at Del Mar and expects more pace help here.
- **King of Gosford:** He won the Del Mar Mile after taking the Wickerr Stakes on the lead, so he can win either on the front end or from off the pace. He has a Rispoli/Damato rider-trainer combination and was listed at 8-5.
- **El Potente:** He has won six of 10 turf starts at Santa Anita and was beaten only a neck for third in the Del Mar Mile after starting from the outside in a field of 11. He was listed at 9-5. He is the horse most suited to this course.
- **Irish Aces and Teao:** Irish Aces was second and third in Grade 2 turf stakes at Woodbine, and Teao is a multiple Group 1 winner from South America. Andersen thinks either can finish in the first three. Irish Aces was listed at 6-1.
- **Cabo Spirit:** listed at 6-1. He is the likely pace, and how fast he goes decides whether Detain gets his setup.

**Pace read:** This is a small field with limited speed: Cabo Spirit is the main pacesetter, and El Potente and King of Gosford can also sit close. A moderate pace favors King of Gosford and El Potente. A real pace favors the closer Detain.

**Card-building takeaways**
- The top three (King of Gosford, El Potente, Detain) are tightly matched and every source ranks them differently. That favors an exacta or trifecta box over a single win bet.
- King of Gosford and El Potente should be short prices. Detain may offer the best value of the three for a win bet.
- Irish Aces is the logical fourth horse to add for trifecta coverage or an underneath spot.
- BettingNews's suggested plays were a win bet on King of Gosford and an exacta of King of Gosford over Irish Aces and El Potente.

**Caveats:** Only one source listed odds, so treat them as approximate and check late odds and scratches at post time. One TwinSpires page still lists Race 3 as a 5½-furlong claimer, but that appears to be stale. The DRF, Xpressbet, BettingNews and Runaway Horse sources all agree Race 3 is the City of Hope Mile.

**Santa Anita Race 4 — Saturday 9/26/2026**

**Race conditions:** Post time 2:38 PM PT, 6½ furlongs on dirt, field of 6. DRF describes it as an allowance race in which some runners are entered for a $50,000 claiming tag; BettingNews lists it as $50k claiming. (One TwinSpires page showed a different Race 4, a maiden turf route, but it appears outdated. Both day-of handicappers agree on the 6½-furlong dirt sprint.)

**Consensus: Liam Smith on top, Clouseau second**

Two published handicappers (DRF's Steve Andersen and BettingNews) both rank the race **Liam Smith – Clouseau – For All Mankind** in that order. BettingNews also uses Captain Shreve fourth.

**Liam Smith (consensus top pick, likely odds-on or near even money)**
- DRF expects him to be a strong favorite. He won by 12 lengths in a $50,000 claimer for 3-year-olds at Del Mar on Aug. 27 and was claimed that day by Peter Miller.
- He may go straight to the lead and repeat that performance. His likely early rival is San Saba, who showed speed winning a maiden race for Bob Baffert in his last start, back in January 2025.
- Risk: he is stepping out of 3-year-old company, and a speed duel is possible.

**Clouseau (second choice, upset candidate, about 5-2 morning line)**
- DRF sees a case for an upset. He lost by a neck at a mile at Del Mar on Aug. 22 to Pure Madness, who is entered in today's Eddie D Stakes. He has won 9 of 32 starts.
- He could get a good stalking trip if Liam Smith goes to the lead as expected.
- BettingNews calls him consistent enough for this level, notes the Papaprodromou barn is in form, and says Rispoli keeps the mount.

**For All Mankind (third, about 6-1 morning line)**
- He benefits if the pace gets hot. He was second by a half-length after a wide trip in a $40,000 claimer at 6 furlongs at Del Mar on Aug. 21, and is entered for the $50,000 tag here.
- BettingNews says he has the best late-pace figure in the field, at 101.

**Captain Shreve (longshot, about 15-1)**
- BettingNews notes his figures have improved in three straight races and are competitive with the field. Neither source picks him to win.

**San Saba (pace factor)**
- He is off since early 2025 and is likely to press Liam Smith early. That early pressure could set things up for the closers. Neither source ranks him in its top picks.

**Pace scenario**
Liam Smith is expected to lead, with San Saba possibly pressing. If they duel, it helps the stalker Clouseau and the closer For All Mankind. If Liam Smith gets loose on the lead, he could run away with it.

**Published betting angles**
- BettingNews trifecta: Liam Smith and Clouseau to win; Liam Smith, Clouseau, For All Mankind, and Captain Shreve second; the same four third.
- BettingNews recommends a win bet on Liam Smith, although its listed odds for him are inconsistent (1-1 in one place, 5-2 in another).

**Structuring ideas for the card**
- **Favorite-driven:** Win on Liam Smith (short price), plus an exacta with Liam Smith and Clouseau in both directions.
- **Value angle:** Win or place on Clouseau, backing the pace-meltdown scenario.
- **Exotics:** Trifecta with Liam Smith and Clouseau on top and For All Mankind and Captain Shreve underneath. This field is small, so expect short exotic payouts.
- **Pass or small play:** With a heavy favorite in a 6-horse field, win value is limited unless you prefer Clouseau.

Check for scratches and odds changes before post.

**Santa Anita Race 5: Eddie D Stakes (G2), Sat 9/26/26**

This is the Eddie D Stakes, run at about 6½ furlongs on the downhill turf course, with a field of 9 and a post time of 3:10 PM PT. Race 5, Eddie D Stakes, 9 runners, 6 1/2F downhill turf, 3:10 PM

**Morning line (named horses):** Sorrento Sky is the 5-2 morning-line favorite with Umberto Rispoli. Pure Madness is 3-1. First Peace and Sumter are 5-1 and 6-1. Freedom's Not Free is 6-1, and Nesso's Lastharrah is 20-1.

**Expert picks**
- **DRF (Steve Andersen):** Sorrento Sky, then Freedom's Not Free, then Sumter. He thinks a repeat of Sorrento Sky's Green Flash run, closing from well back, gives him a stellar chance in this competitive field.
- **Xpressbet (Jeremy Plonk):** Top pick is Sumter. His plays are a $50 win bet on Sumter, a $10 exacta key-box of Sumter with Freedom's Not Free and Pure Madness, and a $10 exacta of Sumter over Virat.
- **BettingNews:** Pure Madness, then Nesso's Lastharrah, then Sorrento Sky, then Freedom's Not Free. They play a win bet on Pure Madness and a trifecta keyed on Pure Madness and Nesso's Lastharrah.

**Consensus:** Sorrento Sky and Freedom's Not Free are the most common contenders across the sources. Sumter and Pure Madness are also strong co-contenders. First Peace is a class threat, but the handicappers give him mixed reviews.

**Horse notes**
- **Sorrento Sky:** He won the Green Flash (G2) at 7-1, rallying from last of eight, and was third in this race last year. Plonk warns bettors to be price sensitive, since he's value near 7-1 but short at 5-2. He is also carrying the top weight of 126 pounds.
- **Freedom's Not Free:** He is a closer. He won the Daytona here in June by a nose, and his 5: 4-0-1 record on the Santa Anita turf stands out. Plonk calls him a huge threat late. His trainer, Mark Glatt, won this race in 2022 and 2024.
- **Sumter:** His last 4 downhill turf sprints produced a stakes win and 3 stakes seconds. He comes in off a bullet workout. Mike Smith rides, and he has won this race three times. He ran a flat fifth in the Green Flash last out.
- **Pure Madness:** He is 7: 4-3-0 on turf and dirt, but this is his first open stakes and his first time facing many of these rivals. He is likely to be forwardly placed.
- **First Peace:** He won this race in 2024 but ran a flat seventh as the favorite last year, and he is winless in 3 starts this season. Joel Rosario takes over the ride. Plonk has "mixed vibes" on him.
- **Virat:** He is the likely speed from an outside draw. Plonk notes outside posts are an edge down the hill and the pace is light, so Virat could hold for a piece of the exotics at a double-digit price. **Scratch risk:** he is cross-entered in the Great West Turf Sprint at Remington Park on Sunday.
- **Later Than Planned:** He adds blinkers and should be part of the early pace. He is a 3-year-old, and only 1 of 3 3-year-olds in 30 years has won this race.
- **Amorita:** She is winless in 4 downhill turf sprints, and Plonk passes on her.
- **Nesso's Lastharrah:** Plonk passes on her, while BettingNews picks her second. She has been sixth, 10th and 11th in her 3 stakes tries.

**Pace:** The pace isn't expected to be fast for a downhill sprint. Virat and Later Than Planned project to be the leaders. Pure Madness and Sumter should sit just behind them, while Sorrento Sky and Freedom's Not Free will close from off the pace. A soft pace helps the forward horses and the outside speed.

**Card-building takeaways**
- **Core key horses:** Sorrento Sky, Freedom's Not Free, Sumter.
- **Next tier:** Pure Madness, First Peace.
- **Value/exotics filler:** Virat, but confirm he runs.
- **Likely tosses:** Amorita, Later Than Planned, Nesso's Lastharrah.
- **Strategy:** Sorrento Sky is a thin-value favorite, so consider a price-driven win bet on Freedom's Not Free or Sumter and use Sorrento Sky underneath in exotics.

**Santa Anita, Saturday Sept. 26, 2026, Race 6:** Maiden Special Weight ($65k), California-bred 2-year-old fillies, 6 furlongs on dirt, field of 9, post time 3:40 PM PT. This is the middle leg of a Pick 3 sequence, and it's on a 10-race card headlined by the Grade 1 Goodwood Stakes.

**Consensus: Not So Merry Mary** (morning line 9-5 favorite) appears on every handicapper's ticket I found.
- TwinSpires thinks she ran well enough to win last time in her first dirt start, and the Tim Yakteen pick makes a lot of sense. She's a gray Sir Prancealot filly from a family that wins early, with Kimura riding.
- Dean Keppler (In The Money) makes her his top pick. He notes a much-improved second on dirt in her second start, finishing ahead of several of today's rivals, and expects another step forward.
- BettingNews rates her a contender who has been competitive at this level with connections as strong as any in the race.

**Second choice: Savvy Tiger** (9-2), on two of three tickets.
- Keppler (2nd pick): She showed speed and then tired badly in her debut for D'Amato, but switches to the main track for her second start and should be tighter and improved.
- BettingNews (2nd pick): They see her getting loose on an uncontested lead, and note Rispoli picking up the mount.
- Pace note: she looks like the lone speed. That helps her chances but can also make her a trap if something challenges her early.

**Each handicapper's top pick**
- **TwinSpires: Ember Royale** (5-1), a first-time starter. She has trained well for her debut for Jeff Bonde, was a $50,000 yearling with a sibling who won at two, and has two good half-mile works on the course.
- **BettingNews: Pavular** (8-1), their longshot play of the day, since they expect the distance change to suit her. Their order is Pavular, Savvy Tiger, Not So Merry Mary, Her Strut. They suggest a win bet only at 7-2 or better, and a trifecta with Pavular and Savvy Tiger on top over those two plus Not So Merry Mary and Her Strut in the second and third spots.
- **Keppler: Not So Merry Mary**, then Savvy Tiger, then Runaround Sue. Runaround Sue rallied for fifth at 36-1 last out.

**Longshots for the bottom of exotics**
- **Her Strut** (20-1): has been running with this kind of field and holding her own.
- **Runaround Sue:** a late runner, useful underneath if the pace falls apart.

**How the picks stack up**
- **Top tier:** Not So Merry Mary (strongest agreement, short price), then Savvy Tiger.
- **Upside:** Ember Royale (first-timer, good works, fair price) and Pavular (one handicapper's value pick).
- **Filler for 3rd/4th:** Runaround Sue, Her Strut.

**Ways to build the card**
- **Single the favorite in horizontal bets:** use Not So Merry Mary alone in the Pick 3/Pick 4 leg if you want to save money. If you're worried about a first-timer, go deeper and add Savvy Tiger and Ember Royale.
- **Exacta box:** Not So Merry Mary, Savvy Tiger, Ember Royale.
- **Trifecta:** Not So Merry Mary and Savvy Tiger on top; Ember Royale and Pavular in the middle; add Runaround Sue and Her Strut for third.
- **Value win bet:** Ember Royale or Pavular, only if the tote price is well above the favorite's.

**Caveats**
- These are morning-line odds. Check for scratches, the tote board, and the first-timers' post parade before betting.
- One TwinSpires track page lists a different Race 6 (a 1-mile turf race for 3-year-olds). That appears to be Friday's card, so double-check you're betting the correct race.

**Santa Anita Race 7 – John Henry Turf Championship (G2), Sat 9/26/26**
Post time 4:10 PM PT, $200k, 1 1/4 miles on turf, field of 8. Nearly the whole field comes out of either the Del Mar Handicap or Del Mar Mile, and the race helps sort California turf horses toward the Breeders' Cup Turf or Mile.

**Morning line:** Mondego 3-1, Sinsel 15-1, Atomic Age 7-2, Balladeer 20-1, Nitti 10-1, Flashiest 20-1, Atitlan 1-1, Twirling Point 15-1.

**Consensus**
- Atitlan: top pick for DRF's Steve Andersen and Spooky Express; used by TwinSpires and ABR.
- Mondego: top pick for ABR's Noel Michaels; "win contender" for Spooky.
- Sinsel: 2nd for DRF; used by TwinSpires and ABR as the value piece.
- Atomic Age: 3rd for DRF.

**Contenders**

*Atitlan (1-1, Rispoli / Mandella)* – Third start off the layoff; he closed from last of 11 to lose the Del Mar Handicap by a neck, running from farther back than usual. He won two stakes in a row on this turf course in spring 2025, including the Whittingham at this distance. Mandella has won this race eight times. The main concern is price: Michaels says he isn't worth a win bet at even money but belongs in exactas and trifectas.

*Mondego (3-1, Juan Hernandez)* – Fifth in the Del Mar Handicap but beaten only a length after being outfinished at the longer 1 3/8 miles. The cutback to 1 1/4 suits him, he seems to prefer Santa Anita to Del Mar, and he won both the Whittingham in May and the San Marcos in February at this distance. Spooky flags a premature move last out and the rider upgrade to Hernandez.

*Sinsel (15-1, Berrios / Mandella)* – The overlay angle. He was 10th in the Del Mar Mile after being hard to handle early, yet lost by only four lengths. He was a Group 1 winner at 1 1/4 on turf in Brazil in 2025. Second start off a year layoff and stretching out to a better distance, so he should move up, possibly a lot.

*Atomic Age (7-2, Kimura / D'Amato)* – Third at 24-1 in the Del Mar Handicap, beaten three-quarters of a length in his stakes debut, and much improved since being gelded in late June. He can stalk or close. He briefly led near the sixteenth pole before being caught. His trainer admits he probably needs to improve a length or two.

**Pace:** Balladeer is the expected early leader. The top contenders are mostly stalkers and closers, which favors late kick. Rest of field (Nitti, Flashiest, Twirling Point, Balladeer) has little expert support.

**Card-building notes**
- Chalk key: Atitlan on top over Mondego, Atomic Age, and Sinsel. Short payoffs, highest hit rate.
- Value win: Mondego at 3-1, with Atitlan underneath.
- Exotic value: Michaels boxes Mondego, Sinsel, and Atitlan in exactas and trifectas. Adding Atomic Age makes a four-horse box that covers every expert's top three.
- Longshot use: Sinsel in the 2nd and 3rd spots of trifectas.

Check for late scratches and turf condition before finalizing.

8.text:
**Santa Anita Race 8, Saturday 9/26/2026: Grade 1 Goodwood Stakes.** Post time is 4:40 PM PT; it's a $300k Grade 1 at 1 1/8 miles on dirt with a field of nine. It's the key SoCal prep for the Breeders' Cup Classic.

**Consensus (5 sources)**
Nevada Beach, Caldera and Original Sin appear in the top three of nearly every source.

- DRF (Andersen): Original Sin, Nevada Beach, Caldera
- In The Money (Keppler): Nevada Beach, Caldera, Taif
- BettingNews: Nevada Beach, Original Sin, Mr. A. P., Caldera
- Xpressbet (Bernier): Caldera, Nevada Beach, Original Sin, Forged Steel
- FanDuel Research: Caldera top, Original Sin second, Nevada Beach third

Win-pick tally: Nevada Beach 2, Caldera 2, Original Sin 1.

**The contenders**

**Nevada Beach** is the class of the field and the likely favorite. BettingNews lists him at 7-5 and rates his closing kick the best in the race. He won last year's Goodwood but hasn't run since finishing 12th of 13 in the Saudi Cup in February. He's unbeaten in three U.S. starts at this distance, and Baffert has a very strong record with layoff returnees. The knock: Bernier notes he has never won a race with more than six starters, and he's suspicious that the horse has been working since mid-June yet skipped both the San Diego and the Pacific Classic.

**Caldera** is the main value alternative. He comes in off three straight allowance wins, with tactical speed, improving form and prior success at 1 1/8 miles. Those wins came at Colonial Downs by a combined 12 lengths, with Beyers rising each time. Bernier makes him roughly 3-1 on fair odds, expects Paco Lopez to stalk and move on the far turn, and plays him to win only at 3-1 or better. Concern: this is his first two-turn start since April 2025, and he's likely to be on or near the lead.

**Original Sin** is DRF's top pick. He won the Grade 3 Blame at Churchill in May, then rallied from last to run second in the Pacific Classic after a slow start, and DRF expects a solid pace. The counterpoint: Bernier calls him a poor gate horse and sees him mainly as an underneath key in exotics.

**Underneath and longer shots**
- **Mr. A. P.**: rated a contender by BettingNews, bred to handle the added ground, around 8-1. Bernier is cool on him after three dull turf tries.
- **Forged Steel**: won the Santa Anita Gold Cup, but Bernier doesn't think the pace will suit him.
- **McAfee**: will attract money off a big Saratoga win, but Bernier doubts he's Grade 1 quality at nine furlongs.
- Taif, Vodka Vodka and Midnight Mammoth get little support. Keppler's third pick appears to be Taif, based on post-position lists.

**Card-building takeaways**
- The top three of Nevada Beach, Caldera and Original Sin is a strong consensus. A three-horse exacta or trifecta box covers every source's top two.
- Win value is likely on Caldera if he stays at 3-1 or higher. Nevada Beach at a short price carries layoff risk.
- Original Sin fits best in the 2nd/3rd slots given his gate issues and closing style.
- For trifecta fillers, the most-mentioned extras are Mr. A. P. and Forged Steel.

Check scratches and live odds before post. I couldn't confirm a current morning line from the track itself, and the odds above are handicappers' lines.

9.text:
**Santa Anita Race 9 – Sat 9/26/2026: Grade 3 John C. Harris Stakes**
5:10 PM PT post, $100k, about 6½ furlongs on turf, field of 10. The race is for three-year-old fillies on the downhill turf course.

**Consensus picks (three handicappers)**

- DRF / Steve Andersen: Yours Sincerely, Little Opal, Mo' Em Down
- Dean Keppler (ITM): Little Opal, Yours Sincerely, Brave Deb. He named Little Opal his best bet of the entire card.
- T3 Handicapping (BettingNews): Yours Sincerely (5-2), Little Opal (3-2), Run With Liberty (15-1), Surfin' U. S. A. (30-1)

**Top pair: Little Opal and Yours Sincerely.** All three sources have both horses in their top two. They disagree only on which one wins.

**Contenders**

- **Little Opal (about 3-2, likely favorite).** She is unbeaten for Doug O'Neill, and her turf Beyers of 94 and 90 are faster than anything else in the field. Both wins came wire-to-wire at five furlongs on the Del Mar turf. The risks are that she is stretching out to 6½ and may face early pressure from Come On Om and Seeking Attention, both summer maiden winners at Del Mar.

- **Yours Sincerely (about 5-2).** She comes off a sharp five-furlong allowance win at Del Mar on Aug. 2 with a career-best Beyer for D'Amato. She was beaten only a half-length in the G3 Senorita on this same hillside course in May. As a stalker she gets a live target if the speed duels. T3 thinks she can exploit the pace and closes better than anything else in the field.

- **Brave Deb.** A G3 winner returning from an 11-month layoff for Mandella, with Rosario riding. She ran poorly in the BC Juvenile Fillies Turf last time out. The layoff makes her a question mark, but the class and connections fit here.

- **Mo' Em Down.** She won an allowance on this hillside course in April and won her only Del Mar start as the 4-5 favorite. She should sit behind the leaders, which is how she won all three of her races.

- **Longshots.** Run With Liberty had trouble last out and deserves another look. Surfin' U. S. A. could wear them down late if the front end collapses.

**Pace**
Little Opal is the main speed. Come On Om and Seeking Attention may press her. If they hook her early, the setup favors stalkers and closers: Yours Sincerely, Mo' Em Down, and the longshots. If she gets loose, she is the most likely winner.

**Ideas for the betting card**

- **Win:** Choose based on what you expect from the pace. Little Opal is the figure horse at a short price. Yours Sincerely offers better value at 5-2 if you expect pace pressure.
- **Exacta:** Box Little Opal and Yours Sincerely. For a saver, key them over Brave Deb and Mo' Em Down.
- **Trifecta:** Little Opal and Yours Sincerely on top, with Brave Deb, Mo' Em Down, Run With Liberty, and Surfin' U. S. A. underneath.
- **Horizontal wagers:** This race is a reasonable single-or-double leg. The two top horses dominate the consensus.

Check late scratches and the tote board before post. Odds above are morning-line estimates from the handicappers.

10.text:
**Santa Anita Race 10 – Saturday, Sept. 26, 2026 (finale)**

**Race profile:** A maiden race for statebred fillies and mares at six furlongs on turf. Morning-line favorite is Zuzu's Classic Gal at 5-2.

**Consensus top pick: Zuzu's Classic Gal (unanimous across all three sources)**
DRF's Steve Andersen made her his best bet of the entire card. The case: dropping back to a turf sprint after a fourth going a mile on turf at Del Mar last month, and she was second twice in five-furlong turf maidens in June and July, closing from off the pace to lose by 1 1/4 lengths both times. The six-furlong distance should suit her closing style. Dean Keppler (In the Money) notes she has run above par for this level in two of three turf starts for trainer Mark Glatt. BettingNews rates her a major player whose numbers grade out better than the raw figures suggest.

**Main second choice: Acclaim Perfection (on 2 of 3 cards)**
Andersen has her third; Keppler has her second. She's a full sister to multiple stakes winner Kings River Knight. She ran last of nine as the 3-1 favorite at 6 1/2 furlongs on dirt at Del Mar on Sept. 4 after breaking slowly and racing wide. She now switches from dirt to turf for John Sadler, has two decent synthetic works since, and should move forward. Her debut was heavily bet, so the barn thought something of her.

**Other contenders**
- **Sally's Wish:** BettingNews ranks her second at 15-1, saying her figures fit comfortably at this level. Andersen is cooler: she breaks from the rail in her 10th start and can be part of the pace, but hasn't shown she can sustain it, so a placing looks more likely. She's the best value candidate for the underneath spots.
- **Training Good:** This is scratch-dependent. Andersen's second pick is an uncertain starter from the also-eligible list who would break from an outside post if she draws in. She was beaten a nose in a turf maiden in her last start in January. Confirm whether she's in before betting.
- **Helping Hand:** Keppler's third pick. She shortens back to a sprint, third start off a layoff.
- **Stella Blue Moon (8-1):** BettingNews contender. Her workouts suggest she's ready to run, and she's bred for the surface.
- **Blame the Track (10-1):** BettingNews contender, with no class concerns at this level.

**Pace and shape**
There's no dominant speed identified. Sally's Wish may be part of the early pace from the rail, which helps closers like Zuzu's Classic Gal and Training Good, if she runs. Zuzu's Classic Gal is a consistent closer but still a maiden after three starts, so she's a strong single for win and top spots but at a short price.

**Card-building takeaways**
- **Key:** Zuzu's Classic Gal on top (win, exacta/trifecta key).
- **Primary underneath:** Acclaim Perfection.
- **Value underneath:** Sally's Wish; also Stella Blue Moon and Helping Hand.
- **Watch the scratches:** Training Good only matters if she draws in.
- **Reference ticket:** BettingNews plays a trifecta with Zuzu's Classic Gal and Sally's Wish on top, over those two plus Stella Blue Moon and Blame the Track in second and third.

Sources: DRF's Steve Andersen (via VSiN), Dean Keppler (In the Money Media), and BettingNews.
